sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Diagnostic Dilemma
sections.description: This section details the patient's admission, focusing on the misleading presentation of severe neck swelling and proximal weakness. It analyzes why the initial working diagnosis leaned toward infectious etiologies (Ludwig's angina) or allergic mechanisms (idiopathic angioedema), highlighting the specific clinical clues—such as the lack of fever, atypical swelling characteristics, and subtle cutaneous/nail findings—that prompted a shift away from standard differentials.
subtopics: Patient demographics and chief complaint: Progressive neck swelling vs. muscle weakness
Initial ED assessment: Ruling out Ludwig's angina via CT imaging and vitals
The 'Angioedema' red herring: Why histamine/bradykinin pathways seemed plausible yet flawed
Critical physical exam findings missed initially: Periungual telangiectasia, nailfold hemorrhages, and generalized erythema
The pivotal moment: Recognizing dysphagia and subtle proximal weakness as myopathic rather than neurologic

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Anti-SAE1 Dermatomyositis and Non-Histaminergic Edema
sections.description: This section provides the essential background medicine required to understand this specific case variant. It explains the underlying mechanism of dermatomyositis, specifically focusing on the unique pathology driven by anti-SAE1 antibodies. Crucially, it clarifies the mechanism behind 'pseudo-angioedema,' distinguishing inflammatory muscle edema from true vascular permeability issues seen in classic angioedema.
subtopics: Overview of Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies (IIM): Epidemiology and bimodal age distribution
Immunopathogenesis: Role of SUMOylation and anti-SAE1 autoantibodies
Mechanism of pseudo-angioedema: Perifascicular inflammation causing subcutaneous tissue swelling versus mast-cell mediated edema
Typical cutaneous hallmarks vs. atypical presentations: Understanding variable phenotypes in SAE1+ DM
Systemic involvement risks: The link between SAE1 positivity, dysphagia, and interstitial lung disease

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning and Multimodal Workup Strategy
sections.description: A step-by-step breakdown of the diagnostic algorithm employed once dermatomyositis entered the differential. This section contrasts the negative results for common causes (complement studies for hereditary angioedema) with the positive confirmatory tests (CK levels, myositis panels, MRI/PET findings), illustrating how clinicians synthesized disparate data points to reach a definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: Exclusion criteria: Normal C3/C4/C1 esterase ruling out hereditary/acquired angioedema
Muscle injury biomarkers: Interpreting massive CK elevation (>16k U/L) alongside elevated AST/ALT/LDH
